items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: I remember had a record that I loved called “Mecca”

ctx.x: Did you start to notice arrangements, the particular sound of a record and what gave it some distinction from the person behind that we rarely hear about, the cat that arranged the horns and chose the — you know we’re going to put a harpsichord in here and all that. Did that seep into your consciousness?

I don’t think it did until much later. I was really, I mean I was hearing the records on the radio and zeroing in on them and certainly learning the arrangements because I was reproducing them on piano as a kid. Instead of practicing my piano lesson I’d start to hear these simple songs on the radio and find that I could play them all with just three and four chords just like a guitar-playing kid of today you know I learned those four chords and then I would also play the melody in my right hand, very simple but…
Me too. I wanted to be Fred Lipsius.
